stages.title: Emerging and developing economies: FDI and joint ventures
stages.sub: After this, you can weigh up FDI promotion and joint ventures as strategies for development, and link trade liberalisation to FDI inflows.

steps.q: A government attracts a huge foreign car plant. The plant sends most of its profits back to the parent company abroad every year, and can pack up and leave whenever costs rise elsewhere. What has the host country gained less control over than it hoped?
steps.right: Its own money and its own industry
steps.wrong: Its exchange rate against other currencies
steps.hint: Think about who actually owns the profits and the decision to stay or leave.

steps.q: Instead of letting a foreign firm own a factory outright, a government requires it to set up the factory jointly with a local firm, sharing ownership and decisions. What kind of arrangement is this?
steps.wrong: A total ban on foreign ownership
steps.hint: Neither side owns it alone; both sides run it together.
steps.pre: Requiring foreign firms to partner with local ones is called

steps.q: In this partnership, local managers work alongside the foreign firm's engineers and learn their production methods, while still keeping half the profits inside the country. What does the local economy gain from this?
steps.wrong: Full control of the foreign firm's other factories
steps.hint: Compare this to a foreign firm operating completely alone: what extra does sharing ownership bring locally?

steps.q: The foreign firm now insists on a say in local hiring and pricing decisions, and disagreements slow down every major decision, since neither partner has full control. What problem has this partnership created?
steps.wrong: Complete loss of profits to the foreign firm
steps.hint: Two decision-makers instead of one: what does that do to speed and agreement?

steps.q: A country removes its import tariffs and quotas. Foreign firms now find it much cheaper to bring in machinery and set up factories to sell both locally and abroad. What is this country now more likely to receive from abroad?
steps.right: More inflows of foreign investment and technology
steps.wrong: More capital flight out of the country
steps.hint: Fewer barriers to trade make the country a more attractive place for foreign firms to invest, not less.
